findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(i) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink, where it could be contaminated by food debris or water splashes. CORRECTED: PIC moved the cutting board up above onto the drying rack during the inspection. Ensure that cutting boards are always stored in a position that does not pose the risk of contamination.
(ii) Observed that the baffles inside the ice machine contained a buildup of soil residues. PIC and inspector discussed the establishment’s regular cleaning schedule, but found that the baffles had not been on the cleaning schedule. Inspector will Follow Up with the establishment to confirm that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch. findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed foods in the clear door sliding cooler had internal temperatures above 41F. The following temperatures were recorded with a probe thermometer: humus 48F, humus cups 50F, feta-cheese spinach pie 49F, cut leafy greens 54F, gyro sauce (sour cream base) 54F, feta cheese 51F, kasseri cheese 51F, and mozzarella cheese 51F. There were hamburger patties that had an internal temperature of 44F that were immediately moved into another cooler. All foods had been inside the cooler since at least 11am this morning (some of the foods had been inside the cooler overnight) meaning the 4 hour time-as-control window had passed when the foods were discarded after 3pm. All temperature control for safety (TCS) foods (other than the hamburger patties) were discarded during the inspection. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain in the cooler (such as non-TCS vegetables and sauces). The PIC will be scheduling service for the cooler. Until the cooler is serviced and functioning properly the cooler will not be used to store TCS foods. The inspector will follow-up on 5/30/2025 to ensure that the sliding cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A box of lidocaine was stored above packages of buns on the shelf below. Narcotic medications are poisonous materials that may contaminate foods in the facility. Ensure that personal medications are stored in a designated area away from food and food-contact surfaces. The box of medication was immediately removed from this shelf. Inspector discussed proper storage with operator who agreed to ensure that medications are stored away from food/food-contact surfaces. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Several nonfood-contact surfaces in the facility require a thorough cleaning. These areas including the backs/sides of counters and fryers, shelving around the food preparation areas, and all hard-to-reach areas of equipment. There is a large amount of food and grease accumulating at the rear of the fryers. Clean all shelving. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent accumulations form occurring. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 08/16/2022.

The building is in a general state of disrepair. Operator states that a vehicle drove into the wall by the drive thru causing the damage to the interior wall and is slated to be repaired shortly. Between now and the next routine inspection in 2024, work toward repairing all holes in walls, ceilings and base coving to ensure surfaces are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable and in good repair. All walls and ceilings must be sealed and any loose/peeling material must be replaced/repaired.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 08/16/2022. 

Throughout the facility there is a significant accumulation of residue/debris from frequent use. Hard-to-reach areas and nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment are in need of a thorough cleaning to remove grease and food debris. The areas behind the fryers is heavily soiled and needs extra attention. To the left of the fryer hood, in the corner where the hood meets the wall/ceiling is a large amount of grease accumulation. Walls throughout the facility have visible food splash. Ensure that all areas of the facility are deep cleaned to prevent further accumulations. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.comment:

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The rear double door upright cooler was observed to have a temperature on the outside temperature readout of greater than 60 degrees. The air coming from the vents felt lukewarm. Food within the cooler was all below 50 degrees but greater than 41. Operator states the temperature was at 41 degrees this morning when checked. Food was removed from the coolers and placed in other, properly functioning coolers until the uprights can be repaired. Corrected on site.  

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Foods throughout the facility were without date marks. This is a repeat violation from 06/05/2021. All foods must be properly date marked if not intended to be used within 24 hours. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The area around the triple sink is heavily soiled. Deep clean the area around the sink to remove residue and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulking is damaged and missing in areas around the bathroom sink. Re-caulk the sink to ensure the area is smooth, durable, easily cleanable and non-absorbent. 

Caulking is missing around the mop sink. Re-caulk around the mop sink to ensure the area is smooth, durable, easily cleanable and non-absorbent. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no CFPM present during inspection. Employee’s stated that during COVID-19 pandemic, class could not be taken. That is correct; however, the employee’s at the facility were all food handler’s only. The employee’s could not prove expired CFPM’s training. Ensure a CFPM is present during all hours of operation. Provided class information sheet during inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Discussed with owner on the phone. Provided new copy of the agreement. Ensure all employee’s understand the content of the document and sign. Keep documents in a public health folder at the facility. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/14/19. Inspector will follow-up on 6/15/21.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Observed open container beverage next to prep table. Discussed utilizing closed beverage container with lid and straw. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to improperly wash hands. A barrier must be used to turn off faucet handles such as a paper towel. No barrier was utilized. Discussed proper hand washing technique with employee’s COS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands – except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved. 

(REPEAT) Observed no single-use gloves being utilized for RTE food contact. Inspector had to ask employee’s to provide single-use gloves for the toppings at the prep table. Cease bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods and utilize single-use gloves. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/14/19.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed interior of back ice machine to have a large accumulation of mold on the baffles. Inspector showed employee exactly where mold build-up was occurring. Wash, rinse, and sanitize ice machine as often as needed to prevent mold accumulation. Inspector will follow-up on 6/15/21 to observe a washed, rinsed, and sanitized ice machine.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed no date marking throughout the facility. The following items were observed to have no date within the reach-in cooler and bottom prep cooler: diced tomatoes, hamburger patties, chicken gyro meat, spinach pies. Employee could tell the inspector when the items were prepped. Ensure date marking is occurring throughout the facility and discard food items within 7 days. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed interior of the chest freezer to have an accumulation of frost. Defrost the freezer and ensure frost and ice build-up does not occur. Clean as frequently as needed.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no bleach test strips at the facility. Ensure facility has a way to measure sanitizer. Inspector will follow-up on 6/15/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed interior of the microwave to have large accumulation of build-up, food splash, and debris - wash, rinse, and sanitize frequently. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/14/19.

Observed the plastic covers over the dish drying racks and the metal storage cart (with condiments near the back window/next to the reach-in cooler) to have debris and dirt on them. Wash, rinse, and sanitize as needed to prevent dirt.

Observed ceiling fans in kitchen to have large accumulation of dust. Wash, rinse, and sanitize fans as needed to prevent dust accumulation on nonfood-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed mop to be sitting within the mop bucket. Hang mops in a manner that allows to drip and/or air dry. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed multiple food handlers licenses to be expired (1+ Expiration - before COVID-19 pandemic). Discussed keeping active food handlers licenses with employees. Ensure employees re-take class online before next routine inspection and provide copies of licensure.
